question.text: The set representing the correct order of ionic radius is

solution.text:
In general the ionic radius increases on moving from top to bottom in group and decreases on moving from left to right in period. So, Na+ > Li+ and Mg2+ > Be2+. 

The size of Mg2+ is however smaller than Li+. Despite the Mg atom having a slightly larger atomic size, the Mg2+ ion is marginally smaller in size than the Li+ ion because of its higher nuclear charge

Hence, the correct trend is

Na0.98Å+>Li0.68Å+>Mg0.65Å2+>Be0.62Å2+

question.text: The values of electronegativity of atom <math><mtext>A</mtext></math> and <math><mtext>B</mtext></math> are 1.20 and 4.0 respectively. The percentage of ionic character of <math><mtext>A</mtext><mo>-</mo><mtext>B</mtext></math> bond is nearly

solution.text:
% ionic character of a bond is determined with the help of Hanny-Smith's equation.

% ionic characters =1.6( ΔEN )+3.5 ( ΔEN ) 2

Where,  ΔEN  = difference of electronegativity =

4.0−1.2 = 2.80

So, % ionic character =1.6( 2.80 )+3.5 ( 2.80 ) 2 =72.24%

question.text: In graph of atomic volume versus atomic weight, the elements corresponding to peaks in the curve belong to

solution.text:
If we see the atomic mass versus atomic volume curve, we will notice the following features:

  • Alkali metals such as Na, K, Rb which have similar properties occur as peaks of the curve.
  • Halogen elements like F, Cl, Br, which have similar properties occur at the rising or the ascending part of the curve.
  • Noble gases such as Ne, Ar, Kr which have similar properties occur just before the alkali elements.
  • Hydrogen and Helium seem to be exception to the rule.

c 113=Rn 5f146d107s27p1= Due to inert pair effect 7 s 2 electron do not take part in bond formation, so, most stable oxidation state is +1.

question.text: The effective nuclear charge of an element with three valence electrons is 2.60. What is the minimum atomic number of the element?

solution.text:
As effective nuclear charge is 2.60 and valence shell contain 3 electrons so the minimum number of main shells for the given element are two i.e., (n = 2) and its configuration will be 1s2,2s2,2p1 .

Hence the given element has 5 electrons in all.

Also, for a neutral atom.

As number of electrons = atomic number = 5.

Thus, the atomic number of the element is 5.

question.text:
The correct decreasing order of electropositive character among the following elements is :

Fe, Sc, Rb, Br, Te, F, Ca

options.text: Fe > Sc > Rb > Br > Te > F > Ca
Ca > Rb > Sc > Fe > Te > F > Br
Rb > Ca > Sc > Fe > Br > Te > F
Rb > Ca > Sc > Fe > Te > Br > F

solution.text:
(i)  Alkali and alkaline earth metals are most electro-positive. Alkali metals are more electropositive than alkaline earth metals.

(ii)  In d-block series, the elements near alkaline earth metals are more electropositive than rest of the members.

(iii)  Metalloids are less electropositive than metals.

(iv) Halogens (Non-metals) are least electropositive. In halogen group, electropositive character increases as atomic number increases.

question.text:
How many of these elements have more first ionization energy then boron
Li,Be,C,N,O,F,Ne .

solution.text:
Here the order of first ionization energy is as follows
Ne>F>N>O>C>Be>B>Li
Hence six elements have more first ionization energy then boron.

(iii) D is an alkaline earth metal

solution.text:
Atomic number of B=Z  and is a noble gas

Atomic number of A=Z-1 (i.e., is a Halogen)

Atomic number C,=Z+1 (i.e., is a alkali metal)

At number of D=Z+2 (i.e., alkaline earth metal)
